parameters.content:
## Update WordPress plugins and themes via SSH with automatic rollback

Plugin updates break WordPress sites. This workflow updates every plugin and theme **one at a time**, checks the site after each update and **rolls back automatically** if something breaks.

### Who's it for
Freelancers, agencies and site owners who manage WordPress sites with SSH access and want safe, unattended updates.

### How it works
1. Every Monday at 4 AM (or manually), the workflow connects via SSH, backs up the database and lists all available updates. If the site is already broken, it stops without changing anything.
2. For each plugin and theme: back up the folder, update it with WP-CLI, then check HTTP status, the WordPress error page, WordPress boot and new PHP fatal errors in the debug log.
3. If a check fails, the backup is restored and the site is verified again. Rolled-back items get one more attempt at the end.
4. Groq analyzes every failure and suggests a next step.
5. You receive an HTML email report. If a rollback fails, an emergency email goes out instead.

### How to set up
1. Copy `selfheal.sh` from the GitHub repository (link below) to `~/wp-selfheal/selfheal.sh` on your server.
2. Open **Configuration** and set `siteUrl`, `wpPath` and the mail addresses.
3. Add your SSH (private key) credential to all 6 SSH nodes, plus SMTP and Groq.
4. Run it manually against a staging site first, then activate it.

### Requirements
- SSH access with WP-CLI, PHP-CLI, curl and tar on the server
- SMTP account
- Groq API key (free tier works)

### How to customize the workflow
- Change `checkPaths` to test more pages after each update.
- Adjust `keepDays` and `maxAttempts`, or the schedule in **Every Monday 4 AM**.
- Swap the Groq node for any other chat model.

Full documentation: https://github.com/Christianzimpel/n8n-wp-self-healing-update-agent

### 3. Update and check
Backup → WP-CLI update → check pages (HTTP status, WordPress error page) → check WordPress boot and new PHP fatal errors.

Only **new** fatal errors, 5xx responses or the error page trigger a rollback. Warnings only go into the report.

### 1. Preparation
Loads your settings, checks that the helper script is on the server, backs up the database, turns on a temporary debug log and lists available updates.

If the site is already broken, the run stops here and nothing is changed.

### 2. One update at a time
Each plugin and theme runs through the loop on its own, so one bad update never affects the others.

Rolled-back items get a second attempt after all others.

### 4. Rollback
Restores the plugin or theme folder from the backup and checks the site again.

### 5. Emergency
If the site is still broken after a rollback, all further updates stop and you get an emergency email with recovery steps.

### 6. Report
Restores the debug settings, lets Groq explain each failure and sends one HTML email report.

nodeGroups.description: Configuration, check helper script on the server, DB backup, redirect debug log, fetch list of available updates

nodeGroups.name: Update & check
nodeGroups.description: Back up plugin/theme, update, load site, check logs and WP boot, evaluate result

nodeGroups.name: Rollback
nodeGroups.description: Restore plugin/theme from backup and check the site again

nodeGroups.name: Emergency
nodeGroups.description: Rollback did not help: reset debug settings, stop the run, send emergency mail

nodeGroups.description: Reset debug settings, analyze failures with AI, send HTML report by mail
